mainTopic: Vows of נזירות by comparison (hair, a basket, a distance, the solar year), and why the 'full basket' vow is counted by mustard seeds
overview: This amud deals with people who take a נזירות vow using an image instead of a number of days. A person who vows 'like the hair of my head,' 'the dust of the earth,' or 'the sand of the sea' becomes a נזיר for life. The תנא קמא and רבי disagree about whether he shaves every thirty days. A person who vows 'the fill of the basket' is asked what he meant. If he had nothing specific in mind, we picture the basket full of tiny mustard seeds, and he is a נזיר for life. A vow 'from here to a certain place' is measured by the days of travel, and a vow 'like the days of the solar year' means 365 separate terms. The גמרא then asks why we picture mustard seeds and not big cucumbers that would give him a way out. חזקיה answers that the משנה follows רבי שמעון, who treats a doubtful נזירות strictly, as in the ברייתא about the lost grain pile. רבי יוחנן says that even רבי יהודה agrees here, because this man surely became a נזיר. The גמרא then challenges רבי יוחנן, and the discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Vowing like hair, dust, or sand makes him a lifelong nazir
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא rules that someone who says 'I am a נזיר like the hair of my head, the dust of the earth, or the sand of the sea' is a נזיר forever, and he shaves once every thirty days.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If someone says, 'I am a נזיר like the hair of my head,' or 'like the dust of the earth,' or 'like the sand of the sea,' he is a נזיר forever, and he shaves once every thirty days.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה opens with a person who compares his נזירות to things that cannot be counted, and the תנא קמא gives the ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He is understood as taking on a separate thirty-day term of נזירות for every hair or every grain, so in practice he stays a נזיר his whole life. Because each term is a full, separate נזירות, he shaves at the end of each thirty-day term.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה. This marks the start of the משנה text.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: A vow 'like the hair of my head, the dust of the earth, or the sand of the sea' makes him a נזיר forever, and he shaves every thirty days.

steps.title: רבי says he does not shave every thirty days unless he said 'נזירות'
steps.stepSummary: רבי disagrees. With this wording he does not shave every thirty days. Only someone who says 'נזירות upon me like the hair of my head' shaves every thirty days.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי says: This person does not shave once every thirty days. So who does shave once every thirty days? The one who says, 'נזירות is upon me like the hair of my head,' or 'like the dust of the earth,' or 'like the sand of the sea.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי argues with the תנא קמא about the shaving. He then tells us which wording does lead to shaving every thirty days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבי's view, 'I am a נזיר like the hair of my head' means one long נזירות, as many days as there are hairs, so there is no shaving along the way. Only the wording 'נזירות upon me' shows that he is taking on many separate terms, each ending with a shaving.

keyTerms.meaning: רבי יהודה הנשיא, the compiler of the משנה.
'It is upon me,' a phrase used to take on an obligation.
נזירות, the state or term of being a נזיר. Here it signals separate terms.
'And which one is it?' A question the משנה asks itself before giving the answer.

steps.confusionAlert: רבי agrees that this person is a נזיר for a very long time. He disagrees only about whether it is one long term with no shaving, or many separate terms with a shaving every thirty days.
steps.whatToRemember: The תנא קמא: 'I am a נזיר like the hair of my head' means many separate terms, so he shaves every thirty days. רבי: that wording means one long term, and only 'נזירות upon me' means separate terms.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: The vow 'I am a נזיר like the hair of my head' is one long term with no shaving every thirty days. Only 'נזירות upon me like...' brings a shaving every thirty days.

steps.title: Vowing 'the fill of the house or basket': we ask what he meant
steps.stepSummary: If someone vows to be a נזיר 'the fill of the house' or 'the fill of the basket,' we ask him what he meant. If he meant one long term, he keeps thirty days. If he meant nothing specific, we picture the basket full of mustard seeds, and he is a נזיר for life.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone says, 'I am a נזיר the fill of the house,' or 'the fill of the basket,' we check with him. If he says, 'I vowed one long נזירות,' he is a נזיר for thirty days. If he says, 'I vowed without anything specific in mind,' we view the basket as if it were full of mustard seeds, and he is a נזיר all his days.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings a new vague vow and tells us to ask the person what he had in mind. The answer decides how long he must keep his נזירות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If he meant 'one big נזירות,' words like 'big' do not add days, as an earlier משנה taught, so he keeps the standard thirty days. If he had nothing specific in mind, we read his words as one term for each item that could fill the basket. We measure by the smallest item, mustard seeds, so the number of terms is huge and he is a נזיר for life.

keyTerms.meaning: The full amount, the fill of.
A basket.
We check with him and ask what he meant.
Without specifying, with nothing particular in mind.
Mustard seed, a very small seed.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: For 'the fill of the house or basket,' we ask him. 'One big term' means thirty days. No specific intent means we count mustard seeds, so he is a נזיר for life.

steps.title: Vowing 'from here until a certain place': count the days of travel
steps.stepSummary: If someone vows to be a נזיר 'from here until a certain place,' we estimate how many days the trip takes. If it is less than thirty days, he keeps thirty days. If it is more, he keeps that number of days.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone says, 'I am a נזיר from here until such-and-such a place,' we estimate how many days it takes from here to that place. If it is less than thirty days, he is a נזיר for thirty days. If not, he is a נזיר for the number of days of the trip.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives another case: a vow measured by a distance. It tells us to turn the distance into days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We treat the distance as a measure of time, the number of days it takes to walk there. Since thirty days is the shortest possible נזירות, a short trip still gets thirty days. A longer trip gets exactly as many days as the walk takes.

keyTerms.meaning: We estimate.
Such-and-such a place, a certain place.
The number of days.

steps.whatToRemember: No נזירות can be shorter than thirty days. Vague or poetic vows are turned into a number of days, either through what the person meant, the smallest possible item, or the length of a trip.

phrases.english: "I am hereby a nazir from here until such-and-such a place"

steps.mimraCoreRuling: A distance vow equals the days of travel, with a minimum of thirty days.

steps.title: A vow like the number of days in the solar year
steps.stepSummary: Someone who vows to be a נזיר 'like the number of days of the solar year' must keep 365 separate terms of נזירות.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone says 'I am a נזיר like the number of days of the solar year,' he counts terms of נזירות equal to the number of days in a solar year.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives one more case of an open-ended vow. Here the number is clear: one term of נזירות for each day of the solar year.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just like 'the hair of my head' or 'the sand of the sea', the number he names counts terms of נזירות, not days. Since a solar year has 365 days, he must keep 365 terms in a row.

keyTerms.meaning: The days of the sun, meaning the 365 days of a solar year
Number or count
Terms of נזירות (plural)
He counts

steps.confusionAlert: He is not a נזיר for 365 days. He must keep 365 separate terms, and each term is at least thirty days long.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: A vow 'like the number of days of the solar year' means 365 consecutive terms of נזירות.

steps.title: רבי יהודה's story of the man who completed the vow
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה tells about a real case: a man took this vow, finished all the terms, and then died.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה said: This really happened. As soon as he finished, he died.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה adds a true story to the משנה's ruling. A man actually kept all 365 terms, and he died once he finished.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story shows that the ruling was carried out in real life. A vow like this takes up most of a person's life, about thirty years.

keyTerms.meaning: There was an incident; this really happened
He completed

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה ends here: open-ended vows are counted in terms of נזירות, and a 'solar year' vow means 365 terms.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda said:
There was an incident,
once he completed them, he died.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a real-life story about the case from the previous step.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A real case happened where someone kept all 365 terms and died after finishing.

steps.title: Why picture the basket full of mustard seeds?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the 'full basket' ruling and asks why we picture tiny mustard seeds instead of big cucumbers or gourds, which would let him finish someday.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: We picture the basket as if it is full of mustard seeds, and he is a נזיר all his life. But why? Let us picture it full of cucumbers and gourds, and then he would have a way out!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts by quoting the 'full basket' ruling from earlier in the משנה. Then it challenges it: why choose the strictest picture?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Mustard seeds are tiny, so a basket holds a huge number of them, and he becomes a נזיר for life. Cucumbers and gourds are big, so the basket holds only a few, and he could finish his terms. The vow did not say which item, so why choose the harsh one?

Mustard seeds, which are very small
Cucumbers and gourds, which are large
A remedy or way out

steps.title: חזקיה: the משנה follows רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: חזקיה answers that this is a מחלוקת, and the משנה follows רבי שמעון, who holds that a person accepts the strict side of an unclear vow.
steps.simpleTranslation: חזקיה said: This is taught as a dispute. The משנה follows רבי שמעון, who said that a person can put himself into a situation where the doubt is stricter than a certainty.
steps.whatsHappening: חזקיה answers the challenge. The mustard-seed ruling is not everyone's view; it follows רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון holds that when a person makes an unclear vow, he takes on its strictest possible meaning. That is why the doubt can end up stricter than if he had said something clear. Since the basket vow is unclear, we take the strictest picture, mustard seeds.

keyTerms.meaning: It is taught as a dispute between תנאים
Puts himself into a situation
The doubt is stricter than a certainty

phrases.english: Chizkiya said:

steps.terutzResolutionType: Places the משנה as one side of a מחלוקת תנאים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seems to be everyone's view, and since the vow did not name an item, we should picture the lenient option, big cucumbers or gourds, so that he has a way out.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ruling follows רבי שמעון, who holds that a person accepts the strictest meaning of an unclear vow.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the mustard-seed ruling depends on a broader principle about doubtful vows, and not on the basket case alone.

steps.title: The proof: the vow about the pile of grain
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows רבי שמעון's view: if someone made his נזירות depend on a grain pile holding 100 כור, and the pile was lost, he must still be a נזיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the ברייתא teaches: Someone said, 'I am a נזיר on condition that this pile has 100 כור,' then went and found it was stolen or lost. רבי שמעון forbids him, because a doubtful case of נזירות is treated strictly.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to show where רבי שמעון says this principle. It is the source for חזקיה's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the pile is gone, nobody can know if it held 100 כור, so his נזירות is in doubt. רבי שמעון still makes him keep the rules of a נזיר. In the same way, in the basket case we take the strict picture.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא
A pile of grain
A large measure of grain
Forbids

steps.whatToRemember: According to חזקיה, the mustard-seed ruling follows רבי שמעון: an unclear נזירות vow is read in the strictest way, as his grain-pile ruling shows. רבי יוחנן will disagree in step 11.

steps.title: רבי יהודה's lenient side of the grain-pile case
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends with רבי יהודה, who holds that an unclear נזירות is treated leniently, so the man is not a נזיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה lets him drink wine and cut his hair, because when it is unclear whether someone is a נזיר, we are lenient.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the ברייתא from step 9 and shows the other side of the argument. רבי יהודה disagrees with רבי שמעון and says the man in the grain-pile case is not a נזיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This completes חזקיה's proof that the matter is a real מחלוקת. רבי שמעון takes the strict side of an unclear vow, while רבי יהודה takes the lenient side. So according to חזקיה, the 'full basket' משנה can only follow רבי שמעון.

keyTerms.meaning: Permits. Here it means he lets the man drink wine and cut his hair, like a regular person.
A doubtful or unclear case of נזירות
To be lenient

steps.whyThisMatters: These two opinions set up the whole next move. רבי יוחנן will try to show that even the lenient רבי יהודה could agree with the משנה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda permits,
because an uncertain naziriteship is treated leniently.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: even רבי יהודה agrees in the basket case
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that the משנה can follow even רבי יהודה. In the grain pile the man may never have become a נזיר, but in the basket case he surely did, and there is no way to release him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: You can even say the משנה follows רבי יהודה. There, in the grain pile, maybe he never became a נזיר at all. Here, he definitely became a נזיר, so how can we take it off him?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a second answer to the question from step 7, different from חזקיה's answer. He says the two cases are not alike, so even רבי יהודה would make the man stay a נזיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the grain pile, the doubt is whether נזירות ever started, so רבי יהודה leaves him as a regular person. In the basket case, נזירות surely started, and the doubt is only about when it ends. Once you are surely a נזיר, a doubt about the end cannot release you.

keyTerms.meaning: You can even say. This phrase brings in an answer that fits even the opinion you would have expected to disagree.
He has entered (into a status)
To remove it from him
There / here. This is a standard pair for contrasting two cases.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי יוחנן is saying רבי יהודה became strict. רבי יהודה is still lenient about a doubt whether נזירות started. רבי יוחנן's point is that in the basket case there is no such doubt, only a doubt about when it ends.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a key idea: being unsure whether a status began is different from being unsure whether it has ended.

steps.terutzMaskana: Even רבי יהודה agrees here, because the man surely became a נזיר and nothing releases him.

steps.title: Why not count cucumbers and let him go?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן: picture the basket full of big cucumbers or gourds. He surely took on at least that many terms, so after finishing them he should be free.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why can't we release him? Let us picture the basket as if it were full of cucumbers and gourds, and that will give him a way out. After all, we are assuming that what he took on himself is separate terms of נזירות!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבי יוחנן's claim that there is no way to release the man.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each item in the basket stands for one separate term of נזירות. The smallest sure count comes from picturing big items, like cucumbers or gourds. After he finishes those terms, any extra terms are only a doubt about new נזירות. That kind of doubt is just like the grain-pile case, where רבי יהודה is lenient.

keyTerms.meaning: Why?
Cucumbers and gourds. These are big items, so fewer of them fill a basket.
A remedy, a way out
It entered our minds; we are assuming

steps.confusionAlert: The last line is not a new answer. It explains why the question works: since each term is its own separate נזירות, every term after the sure minimum is a fresh doubt.

steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's statement 'בְּמַאי לְסַלּוֹקֵיהּ מִינֵּיהּ' (with what can we remove it from him?)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Since he took on separate terms, he surely owes only the smallest possible count. After that, each further term is a doubt whether a new נזירות started, and רבי יהודה is lenient about that kind of doubt.
